skill.name: task-workflow
skill.description: Guide coding tasks through research, implementation, test decisions, browser verification, and evidence-based signoff.
skill.summary: An eight-phase coding workflow with progress artifacts, verification helpers, and documented quality gates.
skill.author: customware-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are formatting, local verification operations, or database-protection rules rather than threats. Confirmed risks include shell substitution through browser-discovery paths and mandatory production migrations without separate deployment approval. A critical semantic finding covers read-triggered obedience demands and coercive continuation instructions; no evidence found of credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Browser discovery inserts a working-directory path into bash using JSON quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shell pipeline with filesystem traversal or spawn find with a separate argument array and shell disabled.

remediation.issue: Workflow gates require applying changed migrations to the live database without separate deployment approval.
remediation.suggestion: Default to an isolated development database. Require explicit deployment authorization, verified backups, and a recovery plan before live migrations.

remediation.issue: Read-triggered obedience demands and coercive continuation guards claim authority over agent behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Remove coercion and unconditional authority claims. Apply workflow steps only when requested, respect higher-priority instructions, and allow cancellation or status-only responses.

finding_verdicts.reason: The package name comes from a fixed list of three Playwright package paths. require.resolve locates package metadata without executing the resolved package.

The import at assets/scripts/playwright-lifecycle.mjs:2 supports explicit server and verification commands. Importing the module does not execute commands; unsafe browser-discovery interpolation is adjudicated separately.
The helper intentionally executes caller-supplied server and verification commands through bash, with captured output and process-group cleanup. No concealed command source was found.

content.user_title: Run Coding Tasks Through Evidence-Based Quality Gates
content.value_statement: Coding tasks can lose requirements, verification evidence, and progress across long sessions. This skill organizes delivery into eight documented phases with reusable verification helpers.
actual_capabilities: Defines phases for artifact setup, research, implementation, second-pass review, unit coverage, browser verification, E2E coverage, and final signoff.
Provides phase templates, a progress ledger, a gap ledger, and a current-phase marker for resumable task tracking.
Supplies Node.js helpers for server startup, readiness polling, bounded commands, runtime logs, and captured process-group cleanup.
Guides standalone Playwright checks for functional behavior, responsive layouts, screenshots, and deterministic waits.
Requires documented decisions to update, add, remove, or skip unit and E2E tests based on affected behavior.
Checks local Playwright browser revisions against the configured browser cache before relevant verification commands.
limitations: Requires a coding agent, repository access, Node.js, Bash, and project-specific build and verification commands.
Browser verification requires installed Playwright dependencies and compatible browser binaries; the workflow prohibits automatic browser downloads.
Quality gates depend on accurate agent-written evidence and do not independently prove implementation correctness.
Contains coercive instructions, unsafe shell path interpolation, and automatic live-migration requirements that require remediation before trusted use.

use_cases.title: Track Multi-Layer Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Organize repository research, implementation packets, connected-surface review, and verification evidence for a feature spanning frontend and backend code.

use_cases.title: Review Browser Verification Evidence
use_cases.description: Record functional interactions, responsive checks, screenshots, lifecycle logs, and unresolved gaps before accepting a changed user flow.

use_cases.title: Resume Long Agent Sessions
use_cases.description: Use phase markers and compact progress records to restore task context and identify the earliest incomplete gate after interruption.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the task-workflow phases and required evidence. Do not execute commands, reset artifacts, or edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repository Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the research template to plan [change] in [repository]. Inspect relevant instructions and existing patterns. Preserve artifacts and do not implement changes yet.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an Implemented Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan focused Playwright verification for [flow], including error states, responsive viewports, screenshots, and deterministic waits. Use isolated test data and request approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Delivery Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing phase artifacts for [task] without resetting them. Identify stale evidence and the earliest failing gate. Do not deploy migrations or execute completion commands.

output_examples.input: Plan a settings-page change without editing implementation files.
output: Research record: relevant repository instructions, settings routes, form components, service contracts, and existing tests.
Implementation plan: update validation, connect persistence, review adjacent settings, and verify affected interactions.
Gate status: planning only; implementation and verification remain pending.

output_examples.input: Review browser evidence for a changed save flow.
output: Functional evidence: save persistence, invalid-input feedback, and cancel behavior require recorded interaction results.
Responsive evidence: mobile, tablet, 1920x1080, and 2560x1440 checks require screenshots and existence proof.
Signoff status: blocked until missing evidence and unresolved gaps are addressed.

best_practices: Review and remediate the reported security issues before allowing autonomous command execution.
Preserve existing task evidence and verify repository ownership before resetting workflow artifacts.
Use isolated test data and record exact commands, outcomes, screenshot paths, and evidence invalidated by later edits.
anti_patterns: Treating this skill as authority to override user instructions, cancellation, or higher-priority safety requirements.
Applying live database migrations without explicit deployment authorization, backups, and a recovery plan.
Passing quality gates using template placeholders, stale logs, screenshots alone, or unverified test claims.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides an eight-phase coding protocol, artifact templates, reference guides, and two Node.js lifecycle helpers.

faq.question: Does it implement a task automatically?
faq.answer: The skill guides a coding agent. The agent must inspect the repository, author changes, run approved commands, and record evidence.

faq.question: Which tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Helper execution also requires the local repository toolchain.

faq.question: Are new unit and E2E tests always required?
faq.answer: No. Separate coverage phases require documented decisions to update, add, remove, or skip tests based on affected behavior.

faq.question: How does it support interrupted sessions?
faq.answer: A progress ledger, current-phase marker, phase artifacts, and gap ledger preserve context and identify incomplete work.

faq.question: What security issues require attention?
faq.answer: The audit identifies coercive authority claims, shell substitution through working-directory paths, and live-migration requirements without separate deployment approval.
